did.abstract: Labor Arts Archived Website (2007-ongoing) contains the archived website of Labor Arts. Labor Arts was founded in 2000 with the aim to create a virtual museum to display artistic and cultural materials created by and for the working class and trade unions. The website includes digital exhibitions focused on labor history, as well as information on their annual awards and events such as the Debra E. Bernhardt Labor Journalism Forum and Prize, the Making Work Visible Contest, and the Clara Lemlich Awards.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Labor Arts Archived Website (2007-ongoing) contains the archived website of Labor Arts. The website introduces the public to a wide range of labor history through exhibitions, including exhibitions on unions and unionists; the role of art and creativity in social movements; protests and demonstrations, inclusive of May Day; and the history of the working class. Beyond exhibition work, Labor Arts also produces multiple annual events including the Debra E. Bernhardt Labor Journalism Forum and Prize, the Making Work Visible Contest in collaboration with the City University of New York, and the Clara Lemlich Awards. Capture of the website began in 2007, but mostly captured the homepage of the website. Beginning in 2026, capture of the website included their digital exhibitions, digitized items highlighted in the exhibitions, and event listings. The website also has a focus on the history of garment workers and the Triangle Factory Fire.

appraisal.head: Take Down Policy
appraisal.p: Archived websites are made accessible for purposes of education and research. NYU Libraries have given attribution to rights holders when possible; however, due to the nature of archival collections, we are not always able to identify this information.
If you hold the rights to materials in our archived websites that are unattributed, please let us know so that we may maintain accurate information about these materials.

If you are a rights holder and are concerned that you have found material on this website for which you have not granted permission (or is not covered by a copyright exception under US copyright laws), you may request the removal of the material from our site by submitting a notice, with the elements described below, to the special.collections@nyu.edu.

Please include the following in your notice: Identification of the material that you believe to be infringing and information sufficient to permit us to locate the material; your contact information, such as an address, telephone number, and email address; a statement that you are the owner, or authorized to act on behalf of the owner, of an exclusive right that is allegedly infringed and that you have a good-faith belief that use of the material in the manner complained of is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law; a statement that the information in the notification is accurate and made under penalty of perjury; and your physical or electronic signature. Upon receiving a notice that includes the details listed above, we will remove the allegedly infringing material from public view while we assess the issues identified in your notice.

phystech.head: Physical Characteristics and Technical Requirements
phystech.p: Due to technical or privacy issues, archived websites may not be exact copies of the original website at the time of the web crawl. Certain file types will not be captured dependent on how they are embedded in the site. Other parts of websites that the crawler has difficulty capturing includes Javascript, streaming content, database-driven content, and highly interactive content. Full-Text searches of archived websites are available at https://archive-it.org/organizations/567.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: https://www.laborarts.org/ was initially selected by curators and captured through the use of The California Digital Library's Web Archiving Service in 2007 as part of the Labor Unions and Organizations Web Archive. In November 2015, these websites were migrated to Archive-It. Archive-It uses web crawling technology to capture websites at a scheduled time and displays only an archived copy, from the resulting WARC file, of the website. In 2026 the website was re-added to the web archives. The accession number associated with this website is 2026.061.

accruals.head: Accruals
accruals.p: New site crawls are accrued annually.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: Labor Arts was founded in 2000 by Donald Rubin, Evelyn Jones Rich, Moe Foner, Henry Foner, Esther Cohen, Rachel Bernstein and Debra E. Bernhardt with sponsorship from Robert F. Wagner Labor Archives/Tamiment Library and the Bread and Roses Cultural Project. The aim of the website was to create a virtual museum to display artistic and cultural materials created by and for the working class and trade unions.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The collection is maintained by Nicole Greenhouse. Maintenance of the collection consisted of rescoping due to missing captured content, redirects and content drift, missing embedded materials (such as videos or attached Google documents and pdfs), and other materials created by selected entities. The finding aid was created in 2026.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged by capture date.
